finding: Ratios against the rule: time 1.9 to 2.2 (upper bound); memory 3.0 on process PSS, 4.9 counting Android's kernel share, 8.7 on summed RSS (not comparable). Under 5 on the comparable measures, the all-in one by 2 %. Verdict: go for a spike.

rows: - Why it did not boot before: `wf vm exec` reaches the nested `agent-dind` daemon, whose cgroup root is `domain threaded`; Android's init gets ENOTSUP writing `cgroup.procs` and shuts down (exit 129). On the host's Docker (`reporting-service` slot, throwaway branch `spike/redroid-as-reporting-service`, redeployed with `wf ship --redeploy-only reporting-service --ref <sha> --tag latest`; the branch name as `--ref` served a cached compose file for about 5 minutes, so the commit SHA is the ref) `redroid/redroid:13.0.0_64only-latest` boots, with a `binder` container loading `binder_linux.ko` from `linux-modules-extra-6.17.0-1020-oracle`.

- Same page in both: the app's public web export. Browser (Playwright headless shell, 720x1280, 5 runs, redroid idle beside it, host load 1.16): 1.5 to 1.7 s, process RSS sum 593 to 604 MB, PSS sum 298 to 309 MB, PNG 100,525 B. Redroid (WebView shell by VIEW intent, software rendering, 3 runs, load 2 to 3.8 at start): 3.0 to 3.5 s until three equal screenshots larger than the blank page (115 KB against 43 KB), which itself costs about 3 s, so an upper bound; Android's used RAM 1,480 MB after load (905 MB PSS + 575 MB kernel), 1,240 MB idle; ps RSS sum 5.2 GB (double counts zygote's shared pages, not comparable); 171 to 191 % of 200 % CPU idle; screencap 0.68 to 0.81 s; boot 29 s on a fresh `/data` (volumes `redroid-data-c2`, `-c3`), 17 to 23 s on a used one.

- Ratios against the rule: time 1.9 to 2.2 (upper bound); memory 3.0 on process PSS, 4.9 counting Android's kernel share, 8.7 on summed RSS (not comparable). Under 5 on the comparable measures, the all-in one by 2 %. Verdict: go for a spike.

Correction to the rollout note above: the redeploy script that runs `wf secret sync-env` runs in a sibling container of the vm-ops-api image (`siblingImage`), whose `wf` is baked in at build from `nuesslerm/wf-cli:latest`; agent-shell's `wf` is not in that path, so there is no agent-shell-before-vm-ops-api order. The real hazard: a vm-ops-api image built while `wf-cli:latest` still holds the old `wf` would call `wf secret` with a `wf` that only has `secrets`. `wf-cli:latest` was rebuilt from the head on 2026-10-11 (pushed 03:15 UTC) so the next vm-ops-api build is consistent. That build currently fails: `redeploy-self` ends in `trunk_deploy.app.failed stage=build reason=build script failed` within 12 s, three times, while the same script (`buildTrunkImageScript`) run by hand through `wf vm exec` exits 0 and pushes `vm-ops-api:sha-1867d1e` and the watchdog image. Cause not found (the job output is not logged); vm-ops-api still runs `sha-4e0614d`.

Native app on redroid, run 2026-10-11 (head `7b8bee986`): EAS build 30dae6da failed in Gradle (`Skia prebuilt binaries not found`, pnpm skips the react-native-skia postinstall); `eas-build-post-install: install-skia` fixed it, build 30dae6da... Verification on head `d4f246cd8`, 2026-10-11 (task #77): CI on the head: `plan` success, `deploy (mla-tamagui)` success, GitGuardian neutral. `wf ship mla-tamagui --ref d4f246cd8 --clear-cache` 122 s, `wf ship --status mla-tamagui` reports commit `d4f246cd8`, alive, `exp://metro-runner-main:20000`; Metro `/status` answers `packager-status:running`, the Expo manifest answers 200 (2,596 bytes), the tap-through page `http://vm-ops-api-main:8080/expo-go?url=...` answers 200. `wf check --deployed d4f246cd8 --no-publish-eas` failed the first time (tier 3 `Page.navigate timed out` on `/` and storybook) because Metro was recompiling its 17 MB web bundle after the cache clear; fetching the bundle once (31 s) and re-running gave tier 3 pass, exit 0; the generated `docs/plans/fix-d4f246cd` was deleted. A cold Metro after `--clear-cache` therefore needs one warm-up request before the 30 s navigation budget of tier 3 holds. Nested dind fix and Expo Go on the shared Metro link, 2026-10-11 (head `9bb1db125`): diagnosis in agent-shell's nested dockerd: a nested privileged container has `cgroup.type threaded`, controllers `cpuset cpu pids`, and `mkdir` then a `cgroup.procs` write fails (`Not supported`), which stops redroid's init; the agent-shell app container itself is a normal `domain` root with all controllers. Fix: the `docker:dind` cgroup v2 evacuation in the dind role of `infra/oracle-cloud/agent-shell/entrypoint.sh` (processes to `/sys/fs/cgroup/init`, controllers into `subtree_control`). Proven first in a throwaway container from the same image (`android-emulator-dindtest`: child cgroup `domain`, controllers `cpuset cpu io memory hugetlb pids rdma misc dmem`, `child_procs_ok`, redroid 13 booted inside in 65 s), then rolled out in the order vm-ops-api (`sha-c0bc8e5`), image `agent-shell:sha-df62946` built on the VM, `wf ship --redeploy-only agent-shell --tag sha-df62946`; the first redeploy recreated only the `app` container, `--recreate-all` was needed for `agent-shell-dind` and `-sessions` (both were still on `sha-d2b25a6`). After the rollout the same nested probe shows `child cgroup.type=domain` and `child_procs_ok`. Redroid 14 (`14.0.0_64only-latest`) inside agent-shell's docker, 1.5 CPUs, adb on the bridge address from `wf vm exec`: boot to `sys.boot_completed` 24 to 49 s (49 s included the image pull), APK install 12.9 s (nested fuse-overlayfs; 3.6 s on the host Docker), routes home 4.8 s, storybook 3.5 s, settings 4.3 s, two-sum 5.4 s, five cold starts of home 4.4, 4.5, 4.5, 4.6, 4.9 s, app 228 MB PSS (366 MB RSS), load average 2.6 to 4.0. Expo Go 57.0.9 on `exp://100.112.131.75:20000` (the Metro node's tailnet address): ping 1.4 to 4.5 ms from inside the nested container, so no access rule was needed: the tailnet policy (read through the OAuth client with `policy_file` scope, no change made) is `grants: * to * ip *` and `android-emulator-main` carries `tag:mobile-learning` like every service; MagicDNS names do not resolve inside nested containers (public DNS fallback), so use the address. First run showed `Something went wrong` with a name, then with the address the app loaded and threw `Skia web loader is web-only` (uncaught, Expo Go): `typeof window !== 'undefined'` is true on React Native, so the module-scope `LoadSkiaWeb` call hit the web-only stub in `lib/skiaWeb.ts`; fixed in `TracingCanvasSkia.tsx` and `charts-spike.tsx` with `Platform.OS === 'web'` (flow tests `test:flow:skia` 15 of 15; commit `9bb1db125`, Metro re-pointed by the Deploy leg). Rerun: Expo Go first-run developer-menu screens dismissed (9.2 s and 14.6 s after the link), the home screen text `Blind 75` found 19.9 s after the link opened, Metro warm; against the browser's warm 4.8 to 5.6 s that is about 3.5 to 4 times at worst (about 2.7 times without the 14.6 s of menu screens), under the 5 times rule. VM cleanup, run by a one-shot service in the android-emulator project with the host socket (owner-approved, removed afterwards): removed containers `android-emulator-dindtest`, `-dindprobe`, `reporting-service-spike-probe`, `-spike-binder`, volumes `android-emulator_dindtest-docker`, `-dindtest-sock`, `reporting-service_redroid-data`, `-c2`, `-c3`, `-cold`, and the `redroid:13.0.0_64only-latest` image; kept `android-emulator_redroid-data` (the project's own, in use). The host `android-emulator` project now starts `app` and the flow driver only with `COMPOSE_PROFILES=host`/`flow` (default: tailscale and binder only), so redroid runs on demand. Still open: the spike branches `spike/redroid-as-reporting-service` and `spike/android-apk` (deleting remote branches waits for the owner's word), the native device-lab runbooks, BetterStack Metro lines (Metro never ships logs).
